==English==
{{wp|<dab>}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈflaɪ̯t/|[ˈflaɪ̯t]|a=RP,GA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-flight.ogg|a=US}}
* {{a|en|CA|Canadian raising}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈflɐɪ̯t/|[ˈflɐɪ̯t]|;|/ˈflʌɪ̯t/|[ˈflʌɪ̯t]|;|/ˈfləɪ̯t/|[ˈfləɪ̯t]|;|/ˈflɜɪ̯t/|[ˈflɜɪ̯t]}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈflɑɪ̯t/|[ˈflɑ̟ɪ̯t]|;|/ˈflɒɪ̯t/|[ˈflɒ̈ɪ̯t]|a=AU,NZ}}
** {{audio|en|en-au-flight.ogg|a=[[w:Australian English|Australia]]}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈflaːt/|[ˈflaːt]|a=[[w:Southern accent (United States)|Inland South]],ZA,[[monophthongization|/aɪ̯/-ungliding]]}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪt|s=1}}
* {{hyph|en|flight}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=flying|:inh|enm:flight<id:flying>|tree=1}}
[[Image:MiG-17F Top View.JPG|thumb|right|A [[wikipedia:Mikoyan MiG-17|Mikoyan MiG-17F]] [[jet]] in '''flight''']]
[[File:Short flight of stairs.jpg|thumb|A '''flight''' of stairs.]]
From {{inh|en|enm|flight}}, from {{inh|en|ang|flyht||flight}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*fluhti||flight}}, derived from {{m|gem-pro|*fleuganą||to fly}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*plewk-||to fly}}, enlargement of {{m|ine-pro|*plew-||flow}}. Analyzable as {{suffix|en|fly|t|id2=th}} (variant of {{m|en|-th}}).

Cognate with {{cog|fy|flecht||flight}}, {{cog|nl|vlucht||flight}}, {{cog|de|Flucht||flight}} (etymology 2).

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# The act of [[fly]]ing; the ability to fly.
#: {{ux|en|Most birds are capable of '''flight'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|Bats are born with the instinct of '''flight'''.}}
## An instance of flying.
##: {{ux|en|The migrating birds' '''flight''' took them to Africa.}}
## The [[trajectory]] or [[passage]] through air or space of a projectile, ship, etc.
##: {{ux|en|The space shuttle's '''flight''' was carefully calculated long before takeoff.}}
## A swift movement, especially as to escape; an escape.
##: {{ux|en|The lizard's immediate '''flight''' when startled makes it hard to catch.}}
##: {{ux|en|The judge thought she was a '''flight''' risk.}}
## A trip made by an [[aircraft]], particularly one between two cities or countries, which is often planned or reserved in advance.
##: {{ux|en|The '''flight''' to Paris leaves at 7 o'clock tonight.}}
##: {{ux|en|Where is the departure gate for '''flight''' 747? / Go straight down and to the right.}}
##: {{ux|en| He is taking the 5 o' clock '''flight''' to London in the morning.}}
### The [[aircraft]] used in a journey through air or space.
###: {{ux|en|He boarded the '''flight''' to Miami.}}
###: {{ux|en|This '''flight''' is now boarding.}}
## {{lb|en|cricket}} The [[movement]] of a [[spinning]] [[ball]] through the [[air]] from the [[bowler]] to where it bounces on the [[pitch]].
## {{lb|en|figurative}} An episode of [[imaginative]] thinking or dreaming.
##: {{co|en|a [[flight of fancy]]; a '''flight''' of the imagination}}
# ''A surface that aids in an item's purpose''
## The [[feather]]s on an [[arrow]] or [[dart]] used to help it follow an even path.
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|I|i||page=164|passage={{w|Bassanio|''Baſſ.''}} In my ſchoole dayes, when I had loſt one ſhaft / I ſhot his fellow of the ſelfeſame '''flight''' / The ſelfeſame way, with more aduiſed watch / To finde the other forth, and by aduenturing both, / I oft found both. I vrge this child-hoode proofe, {{...}}}}
## An [[aerodynamics|aerodynamic]] surface designed to guide a projectile's trajectory.
## {{lb|en|engineering}} The shaped material forming the [[thread]] of a [[screw]].
# ''A thing that flies or moves as if in flight''
## {{lb|en|collective|military|air force}} An [[air force]] unit, ranked below a [[squadron]], comprising several planes and their crews.
## {{lb|en|US|naval}} A numbered [[subclass]] of a given class of [[warship]], denoting incremental [[modernization]]s to the original [[design]].
## {{lb|en|collective}} A group of birds, especially [[dove]]s ([[pigeon]]s), [[goshawk]]s or [[swallow]]s.
##: {{ux|en|a '''flight''' of swallows}}
##: {{syn|en|flock}}
## {{lb|en|collective}} A group of [[angel]]s or types of angels, e.g., [[seraph]]im, [[cherub]]im.
##: {{ux|en|The central figure in the painting is a young woman, surrounded by a '''flight''' of angels.}}
## A [[paper airplane]]. {{rfex|en}}
# ''A segment of a whole''
## A series of [[stair]]s between [[landing]]s.
##* {{quote-book|en
|year=1967
|author=w:Barbara Sleigh
|title=w:Jessamy
|year_published=1993
|location=Sevenoaks, Kent
|publisher=Bloomsbury
|isbn=0 340 19547 9
|page=84
|url=
|passage = She crept up the stairs [...] On she went, across the landing, from which sprang the tall window, and up the next '''flight''' until she reached the top.
}}
## A floor which is reached by [[stair]]s or [[escalator]]s.
##: {{ux|en|How many '''flights''' up is it?}}
## A level of a [[terrace]]; a series of such levels making up a terrace.
##: {{ux|en|I'll start on the lowest '''flight''' of the terrace, you start at the top.}}
##: {{ux|en|The '''flight''' of terraces extended up fifty meters from the base.}}
## A group of canal [[lock]]s with a short distance between them
## {{lb|en|sports}} A group of competitors, divided by ability or other factors.
##: {{ux|en|The competing sprinters were divided into several '''flights'''.}}
# Several sample glasses (usually three to five) of a specific wine [[varietal]] or other variations in wine, each sample comprising a smaller amount than a full glass of wine.
## {{lb|en|by extension}} A comparable sample of [[beer]]s or other drinks.
## {{lb|en|by extension}} A series of small dishes of food united by a purpose, category, etc.
##: {{ux|en|a '''flight''' of canapés, a '''flight''' of sliders}}
# {{lb|en|advertising|broadcasting}} An advertising campaign of fixed length.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Pat Fallon; Fred Senn|title=Juicing the Orange|page=34
|passage=After the first eight-week '''flight''' of advertising, the tracking research showed that consumers' predisposition to use Citi as a financial services provider jumped 50 percent.}}

# {{lb|en|cricket|of a spin bowler}} To [[throw]] the [[ball]] in such a way that it has more [[airtime]] and more [[spin]] than usual.

|date=March 14, 2017

|title=Leicester stun Sevilla to reach last eight after Kasper Schmeichel save

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, from {{inh|en|ang|flyht}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*fluhti}}, derived from {{m|gem-pro|*fleuhaną||to flee}}. Analyzable as {{suffix|en|flee|t}} (variant of {{m|en|-th}}). Cognate with {{cog|nl|vlucht}}, {{cog|de|Flucht}} (etymology 1).

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# The act of [[fleeing]].
#: ''take '''flight'''''
#: ''the '''flight''' of a refugee''
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1902|author=John Buchan|title=The Outgoing of the Tide
|passage=But the sight of her eyes was not a thing to forget. John Dodds said they were the een of a deer with the Devil ahint them; and indeed, they would so appal an onlooker that a sudden unreasoning terror came into his heart, while his feet would impel him to '''flight'''.}}
